graph_edits.rationale: Enlarge the carved ground response so the frontage reads as a usable public void rather than a minor subtraction.
Deepen the carve to strengthen street-edge porosity and make the access side visibly legible.
Increase the secondary notch so the ground threshold has a clearer entry seam and public articulation.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant bar that has been bent and terraced into a single continuous mass rather than fragmented pieces, so gesture and hierarchy are reasonably clear. Across the four views it stays legible, with no obvious view-to-view collision contradictions. The stepped silhouette is coherent enough to score above average, but the section is still somewhat generic and the terrace stack does not yet strongly register as a capacity-bearing public section. The main weakness is the access/frontage response: the blue verified road edge is not answered by a clearly public void, undercut, or entry seam; the visible mass is comparatively sealed and the carved/notched logic remains too small to read as an active ground threshold. Programmatically it can plausibly support neighborhood living / mixed-use because the mass is compact, urban, and bar-like, but it still needs a more explicit public ground figure to fully satisfy the semantic brief.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Tall prismatic mixed-use mass with a clear dominant figure and a legible carved relation to ground.
